title: Reduced engine power / limp mode
h1: Why does my car say reduced engine power?
metaDesc: Reduced engine power or limp mode message? Answer a few questions to see if it's the throttle, overheating, transmission or turbo, and how urgent it is.
synonyms: car has no power and warning message
reduced engine power then goes away
intro: "Reduced engine power" and "limp mode" mean the car's computer has deliberately cut power to protect the engine or transmission, or because it can't trust a sensor. The message itself doesn't say why, so the other signs matter. Answer a few questions to see how serious it is and what's most likely behind it.
safety: If power drops while you're in traffic, turn on your hazard lights and steer to the shoulder or a side street.
If the check engine light is flashing, or the engine shakes, pull over and turn the engine off.
If the temperature gauge is in the red or there's steam from under the hood, stop and turn the engine off.
If you smell burning or see smoke, stop and step away from the car.

q_power.q: How much power do you have right now?

opts.a: Almost none: it crawls, can't keep up with traffic, or stalls
Noticeably less, but I can still move with slower traffic
It went back to normal after I turned the car off and on

q_signs.q: Do you notice any of these as well?
q_signs.help: A DPF is the diesel particulate filter, a soot filter in the exhaust of most modern diesels.

opts.a: The engine temperature gauge is high, or there's steam
The check engine light is flashing, or the engine shakes or stumbles
It's stuck in one gear, shifts oddly, or a transmission light is on
It has a turbo, and I hear a loud whoosh or hiss when accelerating
It's a diesel and a DPF or exhaust filter light is on
None of these. Just the message, maybe with a steady check engine light

result.title: Power is cut too far to drive safely
result.now: Turn on your hazard lights, get out of traffic and park. Have the car towed or call a mobile mechanic.
if: If the temperature gauge is high, steam appears or the check engine light is flashing, pull over as soon as it's safe and turn the engine off.
If a red oil pressure light comes on, or you hear knocking, pull over as soon as it's safe and turn the engine off to avoid engine damage.
If you smell burning or fuel, or see smoke, pull over as soon as it's safe, turn the engine off and step away from the car.
result.why: When a car can barely move, it's a hazard on any road with traffic. The computer usually cuts power this hard only for a fault it treats as serious, and pushing on can damage the engine or transmission.

causes.name: Electronic throttle or accelerator pedal sensor failure
causes.clues: The gas pedal does almost nothing, and the engine idles fine.

causes.name: Engine overheating protection
causes.clues: A high temperature gauge or steam.

causes.name: Severe transmission fault
causes.clues: The engine revs but the car barely moves.

causes.name: Badly clogged exhaust or catalytic converter
causes.clues: Power faded over weeks, with a rotten-egg smell or a red-hot glow under the car.

you: Note any other warning lights and take a photo of the dash for the shop.

result.title: The engine may be overheating and cutting power to protect itself
result.now: Pull over where it's safe and turn the engine off. Don't open the radiator cap while it's hot. Have it towed or call a mobile mechanic.
if: If you see steam, keep the hood closed until it stops and everything has cooled.
If a red oil pressure light comes on, you hear knocking, or you see smoke, keep the engine off and don't restart it.
If you smell coolant inside the car or see fog on the inside of the windows, keep the windows open and get it checked before driving again.
result.why: Some engines reduce power when they get too hot to slow down the damage. Driving an overheating engine can warp or crack major parts in minutes.

causes.name: Low coolant from a leak
causes.clues: A sweet smell, steam, or puddles under the front of the car.

causes.name: Cooling fan or water pump failure
causes.clues: It overheats mostly in traffic (fan) or at any speed (pump).

causes.name: Stuck thermostat
causes.clues: The gauge climbed quickly with no leak.

you: Once fully cool, check the coolant level in the see-through reservoir.
shop: Cooling fan and water pump tests

result.title: A severe misfire is possible, and it can damage the engine and exhaust
result.now: Pull over where it's safe and turn the engine off. Have the car towed or call a mobile mechanic.
if: If you smell something hot or see a glow under the car, move away from it. The catalytic converter may be overheating.
If you smell fuel, see smoke, or the red oil pressure light comes on, keep the engine off and don't restart it.
If the temperature gauge climbs, pull over when it's safe, turn the engine off and let it cool.
result.why: A flashing check engine light usually means the engine is misfiring badly enough to send unburned fuel into the exhaust. That can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter, and the car may cut power because of it.

causes.name: Failed ignition coil or spark plug
causes.clues: The shaking is worse when you accelerate.

causes.name: Fuel injector fault
causes.clues: A fuel smell or rough idle.

causes.name: Engine mechanical problem
causes.clues: Ticking or knocking, or low oil.

you: Check the oil level once the engine is off and cool.
shop: Ignition coil and spark plug tests

result.title: The transmission may have a fault that put the car in limp mode
result.now: Get off highways and busy roads when it's safe and have it towed to a shop.
if: If the transmission slips, smells burnt, the car won't move, or you see smoke, stop and have it towed.
If a transmission temperature warning comes on, or the engine temperature gauge climbs, pull over and turn the engine off.
If a restart clears it, still get the codes read within a few days.
result.why: When the transmission computer sees a problem, it often holds the transmission in one gear and limits power. The car can still move slowly, but it isn't built to be driven this way for long.

causes.name: Shift solenoid or speed sensor fault
causes.clues: It went into one gear suddenly.

causes.name: Low or overheated transmission fluid
causes.clues: Slipping, a leak, or towing before it happened.

causes.name: Wiring or low battery voltage
causes.clues: Several warning lights came on at once.

you: Look under the car for red fluid.

result.title: The turbo may be losing boost through a leak or fault
result.now: Drive gently, avoid hard acceleration and highways, and get it checked within the next few days.
if: If you see blue or heavy smoke from the exhaust, or oil around the turbo, stop driving it. A failing turbo can damage the engine.
If you hear a new loud whine or grinding from the turbo, stop driving it.
If the check engine light flashes, the temperature gauge climbs, or you smell burning, pull over and turn the engine off.
result.why: A whoosh or hiss under acceleration often means pressurized air is escaping before it reaches the engine. The computer sees too little boost and cuts power. A split hose or loose clamp is a common cause, and a shop will usually pressure-test the hoses before looking at the turbo itself.

causes.name: Split or loose boost hose or clamp
causes.clues: The hiss is loudest under acceleration, and you may see an oily hose.

causes.name: Wastegate or boost control fault
causes.clues: Power comes and goes with no hiss.

causes.name: Failing turbocharger
causes.clues: Whining, blue smoke, or oil in the intake hoses.

you: With the engine off and cool, look for loose clamps or split hoses between the turbo and the engine.
shop: Code scan and live boost readings

result.title: The diesel exhaust filter may be clogged with soot
result.now: Have a shop check it within the next few days. They can run a forced cleaning cycle. Avoid more short trips until then.
if: If only the filter light is on and power is normal, your owner's manual may say a steady highway drive will let it clean itself. Follow the manual, not a guess.
If the engine temperature rises, you smell burning, or you see smoke, pull over and turn the engine off.
If the check engine light flashes or power drops further, stop driving and have it checked.
result.why: Diesel soot filters clean themselves by burning off soot during longer drives. Lots of short trips stop that from happening, and once the filter is too full, the engine cuts power to protect itself.

causes.name: Too many short trips
causes.clues: Mostly town driving, few highway runs.

causes.name: Faulty pressure sensor or hose on the filter
causes.clues: The light returns soon after a cleaning.

causes.name: An engine fault making extra soot
causes.clues: Black smoke, or other engine codes.

you: Check your owner's manual for what it says about the filter light.
shop: Code scan and soot level reading

result.title: Often the electronic throttle or gas pedal sensor
result.now: Find a safe place to stop, turn the car off for a minute and restart it. Then have the codes read within the next few days, and avoid highways until it's fixed.
if: If power drops so low you can't keep up with traffic, stop driving and have it towed.
If the engine races, surges, or doesn't slow down when you lift off the pedal, shift to neutral, brake to a stop, turn the engine off and have it towed.
If the check engine light starts flashing or the temperature gauge climbs, pull over and turn the engine off.
If several other warning lights come on too, ask for the battery and charging system to be tested as well.
result.why: On modern cars, the gas pedal is a sensor, and a motor opens the throttle. If the computer gets readings it can't trust from either one, it limits power so the car can't speed up on its own. A dirty throttle, a sensor or a wiring connection are common causes. A shop will usually read the codes and test the sensors and wiring before replacing parts.

causes.name: Dirty or failing electronic throttle body
causes.clues: A rough or uneven idle, or it happens more often in cold or damp weather.

causes.name: Accelerator pedal sensor fault
causes.clues: The pedal feels normal but the engine doesn't respond in step with it.

causes.name: Wiring or connector problem
causes.clues: It comes and goes, especially over bumps.

causes.name: Low battery voltage
causes.clues: A weak battery or other warning lights coming on.

you: Note whether the check engine light is on, and take a photo of the dash.

result.title: A fault that clears with a restart is still a fault
result.now: Get the stored codes read within the next few days, before it happens again in traffic.
if: If it keeps coming back, avoid highways and busy merges until it's fixed.
If it happens with a flashing check engine light, high temperature, a red warning light, or a burning smell, stop driving it.
result.why: Restarting resets the computer, so power comes back, but the code that caused it is often still stored. Problems like this tend to return, often at a bad moment.

causes.name: Electronic throttle or pedal sensor glitch
causes.clues: It happened suddenly, with nothing else wrong.

causes.name: Loose or corroded wiring connector
causes.clues: It happens over bumps or in wet weather.

causes.name: Weak battery or charging problem
causes.clues: Slow cranking, dim lights, or other lights coming on.

you: Note the speed, weather and what you were doing when it happened.
shop: Code scan, including stored and history codes
